title: api-robustness-standardize-retry-after-idempotency-streaming-openai-compat
author: Ava Morgan
release_notes: Standardizes Retry-After semantics and idempotency handling across streaming and non-streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints; improves error code consistency; updates SDK compat behavior.
description: Motivation: Customers integrating with the OpenAI-compatible endpoints have seen inconsistent rate-limit headers, ambiguous error codes during streaming sessions, and unreliable idempotency key handling when a connection is interrupted. This causes noisy retries, duplicate operations in function/tool-calling flows, and poor developer experience in SDKs. Change summary: 1) Normalize Retry-After semantics across the API surface: every rate-limited response (429, 503 with transient signal) now includes a Retry-After header with seconds and an X-RateLimit-Reset timestamp when available. 2) Enforce idempotency key preservation for streaming endpoints: the server persists idempotency keys for the full request lifecycle (including aborts and reconnects) and returns a deterministic idempotency status object. 3) Map internal error classes to a consistent OpenAI-compat error envelope, adding canonical error codes and a retryable boolean to make SDK behavior deterministic. 4) Streaming stability fixes: improve ephemeral connection cleanup and KV-cache rollback for partially-completed generation to avoid double-execution in function calling. 5) Tests and docs: add unit/integration tests for retry semantics, add docs page describing rate-limit headers and idempotency expectations for SDK authors. Checklist: - [x] Implement Retry-After header and X-RateLimit-Reset propagation across gateways - [x] Persist idempotency keys for streaming flows and make status idempotent - [x] Add canonical OpenAI-compat error mapping and docs - [x] Add unit and integration tests for streaming reconnect/abort cases - [x] Update Python and TypeScript SDK compat tests - [x] Performance check for additional header overhead Metrics/observations: initial staging run showed a 0.2% p99 latency increase under high concurrency attributable to header computation; mitigations added (caching computed reset timestamps) removed the regression. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag for one week then enable by default; monitor idempotency conflict rates and rate-limit error volume.

review_comments: Samir Patel: Can you clarify how Retry-After is computed when we have both quota-based and token-bucket windows? Are we exposing the earliest reset?

Ava Morgan (author): We surface the earliest authoritative reset we have. If token-bucket estimates are used we add an X-RateLimit-Reset-Estimated header; primary Retry-After is always seconds to the earliest deterministic reset.
Evelyn Ortiz: The idempotency persistence looks good but we need TTL guarded by config so old keys don't blow up KV storage. Add a default 24h TTL and make configurable.
Ava Morgan (author): Added TTL with default 24h and a migration comment; storage sweep is behind maintenance job, noted in docs.

Maya Lin: Integration tests are thorough. One nit: the OpenAI-compat error envelope should include a stable code string for SDKs to branch on (i.e., 'rate_limit', 'internal_error'). Make sure tests assert those codes.
Ava Morgan (author): Added canonical codes and updated SDK tests to assert on them.
ci_checks: integration-tests: fail (flaky streaming reconnect) -> fix -> pass
notes_on_merge: Feature rolled out behind feature flag; default enabled after one-week staged rollout and monitoring. Observability dashboards updated to show idempotency conflicts and rate-limit resets.
testing_notes: Added integration scenario that simulates a streaming generator that aborts mid-stream then reconnects with same idempotency key; server now returns status with existing result when available or 'in_progress' otherwise. SDKs updated to interpret retryable flag and backoff accordingly.
documentation_changes: docs/openai-rate-limits.md added with examples for Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset and idempotency behavior for streaming and function calling. SDK compat guides updated.
rollback_plan: Feature behind flag; if telemetry shows increased duplicates or storage pressure, we will rollback flag and revert idempotency persistence migration. KV sweep will not run until rollback cleared.
impact: Low risk: header-only additions and idempotency TTL prevent long-term storage growth. Expected to reduce duplicate function calls and improve SDK retry behavior.
